The C++ and DSA internship in short

The SkillMe C++ and DSA internship is a 4-week, fully remote programme open to students worldwide. Over four weekly milestones you build one of 3 projects, such as AlgoCore: A Command-Line Data Toolkit, post each milestone publicly on LinkedIn, and have it reviewed against clear acceptance criteria. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month, and interns who get 3 of 4 milestones approved earn a QR-verified certificate and a Letter of Recommendation.

What you build

One of 3 real projects, built over four weeks

You are assigned one of these projects when you start, and build it milestone by milestone.

AlgoCore: A Command-Line Data Toolkit

Build a small C++ command-line tool that stores and searches records, learning core language features and the STL along the way.

  1. W1Structs, Functions and a Console Menu
  2. W2Classes, File Saving and Sorting
  3. W3A Hand-Built Data Structure and Recursion
  4. W4Polish, Bulk Import and a Final Report

PixelForge: A Terminal 2D Game

Build a small ASCII/terminal-based 2D game in C++, adding movement, collisions and simple physics week by week.

  1. W1A Moving Character on a Grid
  2. W2Obstacles, Collisions and Classes
  3. W3Simple Physics: Gravity and Velocity
  4. W4Levels, Scoring and a Polished Demo

DataVault: A Simple In-Memory Database Engine

Build a tiny command-line database engine in C++ that stores records, indexes them for fast lookup, and supports simple queries.

  1. W1Records, Tables and Basic Commands
  2. W2Filtering, Updating and Deleting
  3. W3Indexing for Fast Lookup
  4. W4Multiple Tables, Tests and a Final Demo
Week by week

What each week of the C++ and DSA internship covers

Shown for AlgoCore: A Command-Line Data Toolkit. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    Structs, Functions and a Console Menu

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Write a C++ program that stores a list of student records in memory and lets you add and print them from a text menu. This gets your toolchain working and practises the basics every later week builds on.

    What you learn

    • Compiling and running a C++ program from the terminal (g++)
    • struct to group related data together
    • std::vector to store a growing list of records
    • Passing data by reference (&) to avoid copies
    • A simple menu loop with switch and std::cin

    What you submit

    • main.cpp with a Student struct and a working add/list/quit menu
    • Input validation that survives bad input without crashing
    • A README with build and run instructions
    • A short terminal recording or screenshots showing the menu in use
  2. Week 2 of 4

    Classes, File Saving and Sorting

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn your struct into a proper class with encapsulated data, save and load records to a file so nothing is lost between runs, and add search and sort features using the STL.

    What you learn

    • Classes with private members, constructors and getter methods
    • Reading and writing plain text files with std::ifstream / std::ofstream
    • std::sort with a custom comparator (lambda)
    • Linear search with std::find_if
    • Splitting code into a .h header and .cpp source file

    What you submit

    • A Student class in its own header/source files with encapsulated data
    • Save/load to a text file so data survives between runs
    • Sort-by-marks and search-by-name menu options
    • An updated README describing the saved file format
  3. Week 3 of 4

    A Hand-Built Data Structure and Recursion

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Add a feature that needs a data structure or algorithm you implement yourself, not just an STL call, so you understand what's happening underneath. You'll add a simple linked-list based history log and a recursive search or sort.

    What you learn

    • Implementing a singly linked list from scratch (nodes and pointers)
    • Recursion, using it to implement binary search or merge sort by hand
    • Time complexity basics (why binary search is O(log n) vs linear O(n))
    • Smart pointers (std::unique_ptr) as a safer alternative to raw new/delete
    • Basic exception handling with try/catch

    What you submit

    • A hand-built singly linked list tracking an action history
    • A hand-written binary search (or merge sort) used somewhere in the app
    • try/catch error handling around file operations
    • A short written comparison of binary search vs linear search timing
  4. Week 4 of 4

    Polish, Bulk Import and a Final Report

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Finish the project with a feature that ties everything together: importing many records at once from a CSV file, generating a summary report, and cleaning up the codebase for a strong final demo.

    What you learn

    • Reading and parsing a CSV file with std::stringstream
    • Generating a formatted text report (averages, min/max, grade distribution)
    • Basic unit testing by writing small standalone test functions
    • Code cleanup: consistent naming, removing dead code, adding comments

    What you submit

    • CSV bulk import with a summary of successes/skipped rows
    • A 'Generate Report' feature with averages and grade distribution
    • At least 4 small self-checking test functions runnable via a --test flag
    • A polished README with build/run/test instructions and screenshots

C++ and DSA internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the C++ and DSA internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: AlgoCore: A Command-Line Data Toolkit, PixelForge: A Terminal 2D Game or DataVault: A Simple In-Memory Database Engine. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

Is the C++ and DSA internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. The stipend is performance-based and is not paid to every intern: it goes to the interns whose reviewed work stands out in their cohort.

Who reviews my work?

Every weekly submission is reviewed against that week's acceptance criteria by the SkillMe team, which includes engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn. Work that misses the bar comes back with notes on what to fix.

Do I need experience to apply for the C++ and DSA internship?

You need the basics of C++20, DSA, Problem Solving, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at Beginner level and week 4 reaches Intermediate+. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How long is the internship and how much time does it take?

It runs for 4 weeks with one milestone a week. Each milestone is planned for about 2-3 hours, and it is fully remote, so you work at your own pace around college or a job.

Who can apply? Is it open outside India?

Anyone can apply, from any country, college or year, and we encourage you to. Selection is competitive: every application is read by a person, and shortlisted applicants hear back within 48 hours.

What do I get when I finish?

An offer letter when you are selected, a public portfolio page with every approved milestone, and a QR-verified certificate and Letter of Recommendation once 3 of your 4 milestones are approved. Top performers also earn the stipend and are referred to hiring partners.
